svg.text: Zenith / Startup concept: session splash, login screen, boot
Proposal, not running UI · styles for the three screens around signing in · none of them may delay or hide a failed start, and every one keeps recovery reachable
Session splash · login → desktop (Appearance › Startup & Login › Session Splash)
The card leaves, the desktop fades in
The desktop grows from 94 % as the
card fades; the taskbar slides up
A circle opens from the account
picture until the whole desktop shows.
"Good evening, Alex" and the time hold
briefly, then fade into the desktop.
All four: the desktop is already running underneath; a press or key ends the splash at once; Animations › Off or a slow machine (two frames over 33 ms)
skips it; a session that fails to start shows its error instead of the splash. Logout keeps the short fade.
Login screen styles (Appearance › Startup & Login › Login Screen · who may skip it stays in Security)
One card: name and password, Desktop and Headless, power buttons in the corner.

g.text: Last used is selected · arrows or a click choose another · Desktop ▾

svg.text: Every account as a tile; the last one used is already selected with the password field open.
A large clock and date over the wallpaper; any key or click slides the card up for the last account.
Accounts in a side panel, the wallpaper and time on the rest; good on wide screens.
Accounts lists only accounts allowed to sign in here (not system accounts); an administrator can hide the list (Security), which falls back to the Zenith card.
Every style: the same trusted greeter, the same throttled attempts, the keyboard path (Tab, arrows, Enter), Desktop/Headless choice and power buttons that ask first.
Boot animation styles (Appearance › Startup & Login › Boot Splash · fixed dark: the appearance is not loaded yet)
Logo and a bar that fills as real
phases finish; the phase name shows.
Five dots circle the logo; each lights
The logo breathes slowly; the phase
The logo and a hairline that grows with
the phases; the name shows if one is slow.

Every style reads the same real phases (disks, accounts, settings, network, session) and never guesses a percentage; the phase name is readable in all of them (Quiet shows it once a phase takes over 3 s).
nosplash and the rescue entry skip it; a failure paints the panic screen over it; the serial log is unchanged (System › Session decides whether details show).
The style is read from the installed root once it is mounted: the first phase always uses Phases. Live and installer boots keep Phases.
Requires: style choices in the session, greeter and boot settings; the greeter account list from the account service. Values are illustrative.
